title: Choose the visual world for Growing Minds Science
question: Re-roll round 1. The roll assigned The Programme. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again. Every card carries the product's real content; the sketch is the first viewport's composition, not its finish.

options.label: The Programme
options.lineage: the public-education identity programme: pictogram families on a strict grid, one signal colour
options.thesis: Parent and child drawn as one pictogram family that grows up across the page, set on a strict grid with one signal orange; authority through clarity, never cuteness.
options.viewport: A white ground ruled by a twelve-column grid. The headline sits flush left in a bold grotesk at seven vw, five columns wide. The right five columns are one solid orange field carrying the pictogram pair at architectural scale: an adult figure and a child figure in the serve-and-return gesture. Along the foot, a schedule strip of the four classes, each a cell with its pictogram (crawling, walking, pretend play, a game with rules), age range, name and price; the active cell fills orange. The action is a square black button under the lede.
options.risk: A Swiss grid is a familiar costume for 'professional'; the page dies if the pictograms are decoration instead of a working system that names every stage, state and class.

raised.raise: One repeated instrument rules the row: the same pictogram pair, at the same scale, is the measure of every class cell and section head.
A preview before commitment: the free infant lesson plays as the attract loop beside the enrol action, never hidden behind it.
Records keep their place: a class a parent has finished stays marked in its cell, and the mark never moves.
Asymmetry accepted as the compositional law: the orange field and the white never split the viewport evenly.
Every later stage carries every earlier fold: the curriculum shows each class as what the previous one made possible, drawn into the pictogram's growth.

options.label: The Exhibit Label
options.lineage: the science-museum exhibit label: To do and notice / What's going on / So what
options.thesis: Every lesson is an exhibit label a parent can act on tonight, so the page is a floor of exhibits: try this, here is the science, here is the class.
options.viewport: A black exhibit floor. One giant white label fills the left two-thirds, set in a big sans in the museum's three parts: TO DO AND NOTICE: tonight, when your toddler says no, wait three seconds. WHAT'S GOING ON: autonomy is a milestone and the brakes are years from finished. SO WHAT: Class 2, Toddler years. The right third is the orange action panel with Browse the classes and the free lesson. The classes run as four labels down the page.
options.case: Parents of 0 to 5 live in children's museums; the three-part label is literally the shape of a lesson, so science-to-action is the page's unit.
options.risk: Also where a strong run in this category lands: it can read as museum signage rather than a school, and the black floor needs real exhibits (photographs, figures) or it goes empty.

options.label: The Risograph
options.lineage: a risograph-printed web system: two or three spot inks slightly out of register on toothy paper
options.thesis: The warmth of a school flyer printed by hand: parent and child as cut-paper shapes in two inks that bloom a third where they overlap.
options.viewport: Paper ground. The headline in federal blue bold grotesk fills the top left. Below it a cut-paper parent in blue and a cut-paper child in pink overlap into violet where they touch, large, bleeding off the right edge. A sunflower cut-paper shape is the action, Browse the classes. A spot-colour index rail down the left lists the four classes.
options.case: Holds identification: the handmade school flyer is warm, human, and nothing like a clinic. Loses clarity: misregistered inks and grain cost legibility for a tired reader, and the paper ground sits close to the spent default.
options.risk: Charm can outrun authority; the science has to be set as cleanly as the shapes are loose.

options.label: The VU Bridge
options.lineage: a row of VU meters across a recording desk
options.thesis: Twenty identical needles leaning into the red together.
options.viewport: A row of identical meters as the page's ruler.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a studio desk is nobody's home, and development is not a signal level.
options.kept: One repeated instrument as the ruler of the row.

options.label: The Marquee Row
options.lineage: an arcade aisle of backlit marquees
options.thesis: One lit cabinet per destination down a dark aisle.
options.viewport: A dark aisle of glowing cabinets.
options.case: Fuses poorly: near-black with neon is the product's own anti-reference, and it belongs to the arcade page, not the school.
options.kept: The attract screen previews before you commit a coin.

options.label: The Passport
options.lineage: a well-travelled passport of stamps and visas
options.thesis: The first five years as accumulated stamps.
options.viewport: Spreads of stamps landing at any angle.
options.case: Fuses weakly: milestones as stamps drifts straight into the baby-book rut, and burgundy guilloché reads as travel.
options.kept: A record keeps its page space and never moves.

options.label: The Raku Vessel
options.lineage: a red-hot raku bowl lifted into smoke
options.thesis: An unrehearsed black-and-white skin from fire and carbon.
options.viewport: Firing stages stacked like kiln logs.
options.case: Fuses poorly: parents do not identify with ceramics, and the metaphor (shock, smoke, fracture) is the wrong one for a child.
options.kept: Asymmetry accepted as the compositional law.
options.risk: Dark and brutal for this audience.

options.label: The Orizuru
options.lineage: one square of vermilion washi folded into a crane
options.thesis: One uncut sheet, thirty-two folds, each carrying every earlier crease.
options.viewport: A square diagram centred like the uncut sheet, folds numbered in a margin.
options.case: Fuses weakly: origami is not the parent's world, though the fold sequence is a true picture of development.
options.kept: Every later stage carries every earlier fold.
options.risk: A vermilion-drenched page for a school reads as a craft site.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What parenting-class sites ship, executed impeccably: a warm photograph, a rounded teal button, three proof cards.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and lede left, a rounded photograph of a parent and child right, two pill buttons, three icon cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other parenting course by design.
